AVAS.summary: Atomic valence active space (AVAS) method for selecting active orbitals for multi-reference calculations.

options.name: subspace
options.doc: The subspace of orbitals to be considered for AVAS selection.

options.name: subspace_pi_planes
options.doc: A list of planes defined by atoms in the molecule, used to determine π orbitals.

options.name: selection_method
options.doc:
The method for selecting active orbitals. Options are "cumulative", "cutoff", "separate", and "total".
- "cumulative": Selects orbitals based on cumulative eigenvalues of the overlap matrix. Must define `sigma`.
- "cutoff": Selects orbitals based on a cutoff value for eigenvalues of the overlap matrix. Must define `cutoff`.
- "separate": Selects occupied and virtual orbitals separately. Must define `num_active_docc` and `num_active_uocc`.
- "total": Selects a total number of active orbitals. Must define `num_active`.

options.name: diagonalize
options.doc: Whether to diagonalize the occupied and virtual space overlap matrices.

options.name: sigma
options.doc: Cumulative cutoff for the eigenvalues of the overlap matrix, controlling the size of the active space.

options.name: cutoff
options.doc: Cutoff for the eigenvalues of the overlap matrix; eigenvalues greater than this value are considered active.

options.name: evals_threshold
options.doc: Threshold below which an eigenvalue of the projected overlap is considered zero.

options.name: num_active
options.doc: Total number of active orbitals. Again, this is on top of any singly occupied orbitals if an ROHF reference is used.

options.name: num_active_docc
options.doc: Number of active doubly occupied orbitals. This is on top of any singly occupied orbitals if an ROHF reference is used.

options.name: num_active_uocc
options.doc: Number of active unoccupied orbitals.

CI.summary: Driver for a single CI calculation, i.e. one not run in a loop. This class is agnostic to the solver.

options.name: ci_solver
options.doc:
The solver to drive, e.g. ``CISolver``, ``RelCISolver``,
``SelectedCISolver`` or ``RelSelectedCISolver``.

options.name: final_orbitals
options.doc: Orbitals to leave behind: "original", "semicanonical", or "natural".

options.name: do_transition_dipole
options.doc: Whether to compute transition dipoles and oscillator strengths.

options.name: die_if_not_converged
options.doc:
Whether a solver that fails to converge raises instead of warning. Set on
the driver rather than the solver: a one-shot calculation has no later
iteration to recover from.

options.name: ci_algorithm
options.doc:
The algorithm used for the CI sigma builder.
Non-relativistic options are:
    - "hz" / "Harrison-Zarrabian"
    - "kh" / "Knowles-Handy"
    - "exact": Exact diagonalization
Two-component (relativistic) options are:
    - "hz" / "Harrison-Zarrabian"
    - "exact": Exact diagonalization
    - "sparse": Sigma builder using sparse representation of the Hamiltonian and states.
        Recommended for debug use only.

options.name: ci_builder_memory
options.doc: The maximum memory (in MB) to use for the CI sigma builder. This is used only if ci_algorithm is "hz" or "kh".

options.name: energy_shift
options.doc: An energy shift, used to find roots around a specific energy. If None, no shift is applied.

DSRG_MRPT2.summary: Spin-adapted driven similarity renormalization group second-order multireference perturbation theory (DSRG-MRPT2).

options.name: flow_param

options.name: relax_reference
options.doc:
Relax the CI reference in response to dynamical correlation.
If an integer is given, it specifies the maximum number of relaxation iterations.
If a string is given, it must be one of 'once', 'twice', or 'iterate':
    'once' : diagonalize the CI Hamiltonian once after computing the DSRG energy
    'twice': after the first diagonalization, recompute the DSRG energy
    'iterate': keep relaxing until convergence or reaching relax_maxiter.
If a boolean is given, True is equivalent to relax_maxiter and False means no relaxation.

options.name: relax_maxiter

options.name: relax_tol
options.doc: The convergence tolerance for reference relaxation (in Hartree).

- "original": The orbitals are left in the original basis after the optimization.

SelectedCIParams.summary: Parameters for the Selected CI solver.

options.name: maxcycle
options.doc: The maximum number of selection cycles.

options.name: e_tol
options.doc: The energy convergence threshold for selected CI macroiterations.

options.name: var_threshold
options.doc: The threshold for including determinants in the variational space based on their contribution to the wavefunction.

options.name: pt2_threshold
options.doc: The threshold for including determinants in the perturbative correction based on their second-order energy contribution.

options.name: selection_algorithm
options.doc: The algorithm used for selecting determinants. Options are "hbci" and "hbci_ref".

options.name: guess_occ_window
options.doc: The number of occupied orbitals to consider when generating guess determinants.

options.name: guess_vir_window
options.doc: The number of virtual orbitals to consider when generating guess determinants.

options.name: ci_algorithm
options.doc:
The algorithm used for the CI diagonalization. Options are "exact" and "iterative".
"iterative" runs a Davidson-Liu solve whose sigma build is the C++
`SelectedCIHelper`/`RelSelectedCIHelper`; "exact" builds and diagonalizes the
dense Hamiltonian via `SlaterRules`.

options.name: num_batches_per_thread
options.doc:
The number of batches of determinants to process per thread during selection and diagonalization.
The number of threads is determined automatically from the environment (affinity mask,
`OMP_NUM_THREADS`, `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT`, `SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK`); set `FORTE_NUM_THREADS_OVERRIDE`
to override it.

options.name: do_spin_penalty
options.doc: Whether to apply a spin penalty to the Hamiltonian to enforce correct spin symmetry.

options.name: guess_dets
options.doc:
A list of determinants to use as the initial guess for the CI wavefunction.
Note that this set will be further filtered by `DavidsonLiuParams.ndets_per_guess` using the determinantal energies,
before finally being enlarged to a spin-complete set.
Therefore, it is not recommended to provide energetically disjoint guess determinants, as the higher energy ones will likely be filtered out.
Use `pinned_guess_dets` to ensure certain determinants are included in the guess without relying on their energies.
If not provided, the guess determinants will be generated based on the guess_occ_window and guess_vir_window parameters.

options.name: pinned_guess_dets
options.doc: A list of determinants that are pinned to the initial guess, ensuring they are included in the variational space.

options.name: frozen_creation
options.doc:
A list of orbital indices for which creation operators are frozen (i.e., not allowed to be occupied in the selected determinants).
This is used to enforce certain symmetries or to exclude certain orbitals from the selection process.

options.name: frozen_annihilation
options.doc:
A list of orbital indices for which annihilation operators are frozen (i.e., not allowed to be unoccupied in the selected determinants).
This is used to enforce certain symmetries or to exclude certain orbitals from the selection process.

options.name: screening_criterion
options.doc: The criterion used to screen determinants during selection. Options are "hbci" and "ehbci".

options.name: energy_correction
options.doc:
The method used to compute the energy correction from the determinants that are not included in the variational space.
Options are "pt2" and "variational".

options.name: energy_shift
options.doc: An energy shift applied during selection to target specific roots. If None, no shift is applied.

options.name: pt2_regularizer
options.doc:
The method used to regularize the PT2 energy correction.
Options are:
    - "none": No regularization.
    - "shift": Apply a small shift to the denominators in the PT2 expression to avoid divergences:
        1 / denom -> 1 / (denom + pt2_regularizer_strength)
        Ept2 -> 0 as pt2_regularizer_strength -> inf
    - "dsrg": Use a DSRG-inspired regularization of the PT2 correction:
        1 / denom -> (1 / denom) * (1 - exp(-denom^2 * pt2_regularizer_strength))
        Ept2 -> 0 as pt2_regularizer_strength -> 0, Ept2 -> unregularized PT2 as pt2_regularizer_strength -> inf

options.name: pt2_regularizer_strength
options.doc:
The strength of the PT2 regularization.
Note that the interpretation of this parameter depends on the choice of pt2_regularizer (see above).

If None, the System option is retained.

options.name: apply_random_phase
options.doc: Whether to apply a random phase to the MO coefficients after conversion. This can be useful for testing the robustness of downstream methods to the choice of MO phases.

options.name: rng
options.doc: The random number generator to use for generating the random phase. Can be an instance of `np.random.Generator` or an integer seed.

State.summary: Class to represent a state of a quantum system.

options.name: multiplicity
options.doc: Multiplicity of the state (2S+1).

options.name: ms
options.doc: Spin projection (Ms) of the state.

options.name: nel
options.doc: Total number of electrons in the state. If not provided, it is calculated from the system and charge.

options.name: system
options.doc: The system to which this state belongs. If not provided, `nel` must be specified.

options.name: charge
options.doc: Charge of the state. Used to calculate the number of electrons if `system` is provided. Ignored if `nel` is provided.

options.name: gas_min
options.doc:
Minimum number of electrons in each GAS.
If not provided, no occupation restrictions will be applied.
If the length of `gas_min` is smaller than the number of GASes, the restrictions
will be sequentially applied to GAS1, GAS2, until the end of `gas_min`,
beyond which no restrictions will be applied.

options.name: gas_max
options.doc: Maximum number of electrons in each GAS. Processed similarly to `gas_min`.

options.name: symmetry
options.doc: Symmetry of the state.

options.name: symmetry_label
options.doc: Label for the symmetry of the state.

System.summary: A class to represent a quantum chemical system.

options.name: xyz
options.doc: A XYZ string representing the atomic coordinates.

options.name: basis_set
options.doc:
The basis set to be used, either as a string (e.g. "cc-pvdz") or as a dictionary
assigning potentially different basis sets to each atom (e.g. {"H": "sto-3g", "O": "cc-pvdz"}).

options.name: auxiliary_basis_set
options.doc: The auxiliary basis set, either as a string or a dictionary (see `basis`).

options.name: x2c
options.doc:
The X2C Hamiltonian to use, specified as an :class:`X2CParams` instance
(see its documentation for the available ``x2c_type``, ``x2c_model``, and
``snso_type`` options). If None, no X2C transformation is applied.

options.name: unit
options.doc: The unit for the atomic coordinates. Can be "angstrom" or "bohr".

options.name: overlap_ortho_rtol
options.doc: The relative tolerance for the orthogonalization of the overlap matrix.

options.name: df_ortho_rtol
options.doc:
The relative tolerance for the orthogonalization of Coulomb metric in the density fitting procedure.
If None, a complete Cholesky decomposition of the Coulomb metric is performed without truncation.

options.name: cholesky_tei
options.doc: If True, auxiliary basis sets (if any) will be disregarded, and the B tensor will be built using the Cholesky decomposition of the 4D ERI tensor instead.

options.name: cholesky_tol
options.doc: The tolerance for the Cholesky decomposition of the 4D ERI tensor. Only used if `cholesky_tei` is True.

options.name: symmetry
options.doc:
Whether to automatically detect the largest Abelian point group symmetry of the molecule.
This will center the molecule at its center of mass and reorient it along its principal axes of inertia.

options.name: symmetry_tol
options.doc: The tolerance for detecting symmetry.

options.name: use_gaussian_charges
options.doc: Whether to use Gaussian nuclear charge distributions instead of point charges.

options.name: jk_mem_thres_mb
options.doc:
If set, the Fock builder will have a memory footprint smaller than the threshold.
If None, the the in-core Fock builder algorithm will be used with no special memory limit.

options.name: integral_backend
options.doc: The integral backend to use. Options are "auto", "libint2", and "libcint".

UHF.summary: A class that runs unrestricted Hartree-Fock calculations.

options.name: charge
options.doc: Charge of the system.

options.name: do_diis
options.doc: Whether to perform DIIS acceleration.

options.name: diis_start
options.doc: Which iteration to start collecting DIIS error vectors.

options.name: diis_nvec
options.doc: How many DIIS error vectors to keep.

options.name: diis_min
options.doc: Minimum number of DIIS vectors to perform extrapolation.

options.name: e_tol
options.doc: Energy convergence tolerance.

options.name: d_tol
options.doc: RMS density change convergence tolerance.

options.name: maxiter
options.doc: Maximum iteration for SCF.

options.name: guess_type
options.doc: Initial guess type for the SCF calculation. Can be "minao" (SAP) or "hcore".

options.name: level_shift
options.doc: Level shift for the SCF calculation. If None, no level shift is applied.

options.name: level_shift_thresh
options.doc: If energy change is below this threshold, level shift is turned off.

options.name: die_if_not_converged
options.doc: Whether to raise an error if the SCF calculation does not converge.

options.name: ms
options.doc: Spin projection. Must be a multiple of 0.5.

options.name: guess_mix
options.doc: If True, will mix the HOMO and LUMO orbitals to try to break alpha-beta degeneracy if ms is 0.0.

X2CParams.summary: Parameters for the exact two-component (X2C) relativistic Hamiltonian.

options.name: x2c_type
options.doc:
The spin structure of the X2C transformation. Options are:
    - None
    - "sf": Spin-free (scalar) X2C.
    - "so": Spin-orbit (two-component) X2C.

options.name: x2c_model
options.doc:
The decoupling model used to build the X2C Hamiltonian. Options are:
    - None
    - "1e": One-electron X2C (bare-nucleus decoupling).
    - "sap": Superposition of atomic potentials X2C.

options.name: snso_type
options.doc:
The screened-nuclear-spin-orbit (SNSO) scaling applied to the spin-orbit
coupling. Only valid when ``x2c_type == "so"`` and ``x2c_model == "1e"``.
Options are:
    - None
    - "boettger": Boettger scaling.
    - "dc": Dirac-Coulomb scaling.
    - "dcb": Dirac-Coulomb-Breit scaling.
    - "row-dependent": Row-dependent scaling.

get_1e_property.summary: Calculate a one-electron property using AO-basis quantities.

options.name: system
options.doc: The system for which the property is calculated.

options.name: g1
options.doc:
The 1-particle density matrix in the AO basis.
Should be the spin-free density matrix (dm_aa + dm_bb) for the non-relativistic case.

options.name: property_name
options.doc: The name of the property to calculate (e.g., "kinetic_energy", "nuclear_attraction_energy", "electric_dipole").

options.name: origin
options.doc: The origin point for properties that depend on it (e.g., electric dipole moment).

options.name: unit
options.doc:
The unit for the property value, either "debye" or "au". Default is "debye".
Only used for multipole moments. For quadrupole moments, "debye" stands for debye * angstrom, etc.

mulliken_population.summary: Perform Mulliken population analysis on the system using the given method.

options.name: system
options.doc: The system for which the Mulliken population is calculated.

options.name: g1
options.doc: The 1-particle spin-free density matrix (dm_aa + dm_bb).

write_orbital_cubes.summary: A convenience function to write cube files for molecular orbitals.

options.name: system
options.doc: The system object containing the molecular information.

options.name: C
options.doc: The molecular orbital coefficients matrix.

options.name: indices
options.doc:
The indices (zero-based) of the orbitals to generate cube files for.
By default all orbitals are generated.

options.name: prefix
options.doc: The prefix for the cube file names.

options.name: filepath
options.doc: The directory to save the cube files in.

options.name: format
options.doc:
Output formats to generate. Supported values:
  - "cube": standard CUBE files. For two-component systems, writes
    separate alpha and beta magnitude files ("_a.cube" and "_b.cube").
  - "2ccube": two-component cube files (".2ccube"). For two-component
    systems only, writes four datasets consecutively per orbital in the
    order: alpha real, alpha imag, beta real, beta imag.
Multiple formats can be requested at once, e.g., formats=("cube","2ccube").

options.name: spacing
options.doc: The spacing between grid points in the cube file (in bohr).

options.name: padding
options.doc: The extra space (in bohr) added in all directions around the atoms when generating the grid.
